'''Marjorie Constance Caserio''' (née Beckett; February 26, 1929 – April 19, 2021)<ref name="wcp">{{cite encyclopedia | title=Marjorie Constance Beckett Caserio | encyclopedia=Women in Chemistry and Physics: A Biobibliographic Sourcebook | publisher=Greenwood Press | author=Goldwhite, Harold |editor1=Grinstein, Louise S. |editor2=Rose, Rose K.|editor-link3=Miriam Rafailovich |editor3=Rafailovich, Miriam H. | year=1993 | pages=85–93}}</ref> was an English chemist. In 1975, she was awarded the [[Garvan Medal]] by the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="wcp"/>

==Early life and education==
Caserio was born Marjorie Constance Beckett in [[Cricklewood, London]], England.  She attended the [[North London Collegiate School]] and began studying [[podiatry]] at [[Chelsea College of Art and Design|Chelsea College]], but soon developed a preference for chemistry and graduated with honors in the subject in 1950.  She was awarded a [[Sir John Dill]] Fellowship by the [[English-Speaking Union]] which allowed her to study at [[Bryn Mawr College]] in the United States, she earned an M.A. in chemistry in 1951. Her thesis was entitled "The alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl ''p''-alkybenzoates."<ref name="wcp"/>

For a year she worked at the [[Fulmer Research Institute]] in rural [[Stoke Poges]], [[England]], researching the effects of [[fluoride]]s on [[titanium]], but disliked the work and decided to seek a Ph.D. in chemistry.  She interviewed with [[Nobel Laureate|Nobel laureate]] [[Derek Barton]] and was accepted to [[Birkbeck College]] in [[London]], but was not offered financial aid. Instead, Caserio returned to Bryn Mawr in the U.S., earning her Ph.D. in 1956 with a dissertation entitled "The kinetics of bromination of naphthalene."<ref name="wcp"/><ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Beckett|first=Marjorie Constance|title=The Kinetics of Bromination of Naphthalene|date=1956|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/301972067/5503EC76844D4C23PQ|id={{ProQuest|301972067}} |degree=Ph.D.}}</ref>

== Career ==
Caserio was hired by [[John D. Roberts]] for a postdoctoral position at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. She spent eight years at Caltech, working on 3- and 4-membered ring compounds,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Simmons|first2=Howard E.|last3=Johnson|first3=A. Earl|last4=Roberts|first4=John D.|date=1960-06-01|title=Small-Ring Compounds. XXVI. Nucleophilic Displacement Reactions of Some Halogen-substituted Phenylcyclobutenones1|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja01497a030|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=82|issue=12|pages=3102–3106|doi=10.1021/ja01497a030|bibcode=1960JAChS..82.3102C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Graham|first2=William H.|last3=Roberts|first3=John D.|date=1960-01-01|title=Small-ring compounds—XXIX A reinvestigation of the solvolysis of cyclopropylcarbinyl chloride in aqueous ethanol. Isomerization of cyclopropylcarbinol|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0040402060800683|journal=Tetrahedron|language=en|volume=11|issue=3|pages=171–182|doi=10.1016/0040-4020(60)80068-3|issn=0040-4020|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the reactions of [[Alcohol (chemistry)|alcohol]]s with [[diazomethane]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Roberts|first2=John D.|last3=Neeman|first3=M.|last4=Johnson|first4=William S.|title=Methylation of Alcohols with Diazomethane |date=1958-05-01|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja01543a056|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=80|issue=10|pages=2584–2585|doi=10.1021/ja01543a056|bibcode=1958JAChS..80.2584C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the [[hydrolysis]] of [[diaryliodonium salts]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Glusker|first2=Donald L.|last3=Roberts|first3=John D.|date=1959-01-01|title=Hydrolysis of Diaryliodonium Salts|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja01511a019|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=81|issue=2|pages=336–342|doi=10.1021/ja01511a019|bibcode=1959JAChS..81..336C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the deamination of [[nitrous acid]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Levin|first2=Robert D.|last3=Roberts|first3=John D.|date=1965|title=Intermediates in the Nitrous Acid Deamination of 2-[p-(2'-Hydroxyethoxy)phenyl]ethylamine1|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ja00952a024|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=87|issue=24|pages=5651–5655|doi=10.1021/ja00952a024|bibcode=1965JAChS..87.5651C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[benzyne]] [[reaction intermediate]]s in [[nucleophilic aromatic substitution]] reactions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jenny|first1=Erwin F.|last2=Caserio|first2=Marjorie C.|last3=Roberts|first3=John D.|date=1958-10-01|title=Benzyn-Zwischenprodukte in der nukleophilen aromatischen Substitution|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02159149|journal=Experientia|language=de|volume=14|issue=10|pages=349–354|doi=10.1007/BF02159149|s2cid=10598895 |issn=1420-9071|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

She collaborated with Roberts in writing an [[organic chemistry]] textbook, ''Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry'', first published in 1964.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Roberts|first1=John D.|url=https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechBOOK:1977.001|title=Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry, second edition|last2=Caserio|first2=Marjorie C.|year=1977|publisher=W. A. Benjamin, Inc.|isbn=978-0-8053-8329-4|location=Menlo Park, CA}}</ref> Notable for its comprehensiveness and then-unusual emphasis on [[spectroscopy]], it proved enormously influential in how the subject was taught. Also working with Roberts was chemist Fred Caserio.

=== University of California, Irvine ===
In 1964, Caserio was hired as the second faculty member in chemistry at the brand new [[University of California, Irvine]]. At UC Irvine she worked on [[addition reaction]]s in [[allene]]s<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Waters|first1=William L.|last2=Linn|first2=William S.|last3=Caserio|first3=Marjorie C.|date=1968|title=Stereochemistry of additions of allenes. I. Methoxymercuration and halogenation of 1,3-dimethylallene|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ja01026a032|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=90|issue=24|pages=6741–6749|doi=10.1021/ja01026a032|bibcode=1968JAChS..90.6741W |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Linn|first1=William S.|last2=Waters|first2=William L.|last3=Caserio|first3=Marjorie C.|date=1970-07-01|title=Stereochemistry of addition reactions of allenes. II. Oxymercuration of 1,3-dimethylallene and solvolysis of the derived adducts|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00716a032|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=92|issue=13|pages=4018–4025|doi=10.1021/ja00716a032|bibcode=1970JAChS..92.4018L |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Byrd|first1=Larry R.|last2=Caserio|first2=Marjorie C.|date=1970-09-01|title=Stereochemistry of addition reactions of allenes. III. Free-radical reactions of 2,3-pentadiene and 2-pentyne with tert-butyl hypochlorite|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00721a022|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=92|issue=18|pages=5422–5431|doi=10.1021/ja00721a022|bibcode=1970JAChS..92.5422B |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and bonding and reactions of [[sulfur]] compounds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Kim|first2=Jhong K.|date=1982-06-01|title=Thioammonium ions. Azasulfenylation reactions|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00375a056|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=104|issue=11|pages=3231–3233|doi=10.1021/ja00375a056|bibcode=1982JAChS.104.3231C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kim|first1=Jhong K.|last2=Kline|first2=Margaret L.|last3=Caserio|first3=Marjorie C.|date=1978-09-01|title=Methylthiolation of allylic sulfides. A degenerate [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00487a053|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=100|issue=19|pages=6243–6245|doi=10.1021/ja00487a053|bibcode=1978JAChS.100.6243K |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She was one of the first scientists to employ [[nuclear magnetic resonance]] spectroscopy to study the kinetics and mechanisms of these organic reactions,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Caserio|first1=Marjorie C.|last2=Pratt|first2=Robert E.|last3=Holland|first3=Robert J.|date=1966-12-01|title=The Nature of Sulfur Bonding in α,β-Unsaturated Sulfides and Sulfonium Salts1,2|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00976a014|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=88|issue=24|pages=5747–5753|doi=10.1021/ja00976a014|bibcode=1966JAChS..88.5747C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Smallcombe|first1=Stephen H.|last2=Caserio|first2=Marjorie C.|date=1971-11-01|title=Kinetics of sulfur-sulfur bond cleavage in methylated methyl disulfide by nuclear magnetic resonance|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00751a041|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=93|issue=22|pages=5826–5833|doi=10.1021/ja00751a041|bibcode=1971JAChS..93.5826S |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[ion cyclotron resonance]] to study gas-phase reactions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pau|first1=James K.|last2=Ruggera|first2=Michael B.|last3=Kim|first3=Jhong K.|last4=Caserio|first4=Marjorie C.|date=1978-06-01|title=On the electron-donating properties of oxygen vs. sulfur. A study of the gas-phase ion chemistry of methoxymethylthioalkanes|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00481a039|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=100|issue=13|pages=4242–4248|doi=10.1021/ja00481a039|bibcode=1978JAChS.100.4242P |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marjorie Caserio & Vy Dong|url=https://calisphere.org/item/5054b9a1-e29c-4f31-9c2f-301e05082223/|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Calisphere|date=11 February 2016 |language=en}}</ref> Caserio became a full professor at UC Irvine in 1972, and chair of the chemistry department in 1987.<ref name="wcp"/>

=== University of California, San Diego ===
In 1990, she became vice chancellor for academic affairs at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. She later served as interim chancellor, and retired in 1996.<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uPRB-OED1bcC | title=Encyclopedia of world scientists, Volume 1 | publisher=InfoBase | year=2007 | accessdate=July 12, 2011 | author=Oakes, Elizabeth H. | pages=125| isbn=9781438118826 }}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
In 1957, she married Fred Caserio; she became a US citizen the same year. They had two sons.<ref name="wcp" /> She died in 2021, aged 92, on a trip to [[Mexico]].<ref name="Obituary">[https://www.cucea.org/memorials/in-memoriam-marjorie-caserio Obituary], cucea.org. Accessed February 21, 2024.</ref>
